# Vue Star Rate — Full Reference (vue-js-star-rating)

> Zero-dependency Vue 3.5+ star rating component. Keyboard accessible. TypeScript-first. Half-star precision. Lucide / FontAwesome / custom icon providers. SSR & Nuxt 3 ready.

This document is the long-form, LLM-optimized reference: install steps, every prop, every event, every slot, accessibility notes, performance notes, frequently asked questions, and migration guidance — flattened into a single text file for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and chat-style answer engines.

---

## 1. Summary

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| npm package | `vue-js-star-rating` |
| Current version | 3.1.1 (2026-10-19) |
| License | MIT |
| Author | Pooya Golchian — https://pooya.blog |
| Repo | https://github.com/pooyagolchian/vue-star-rate |
| Docs / live demo | https://pooyagolchian.github.io/vue-star-rate/ |
| Peer dep | `vue ^3.5.0` |
| Runtime deps | none |
| Optional peers | none (see section 10 for the caveat about releases 2.0.0 to 3.1.0) |
| Bundle size | `import { VueStarRate }`: about 4.6 KB gzipped JavaScript (12.4 KB raw) plus 0.75 KB gzipped CSS (2.9 KB raw); all three icon providers included, nothing lazy-loaded. `useStarRating` alone: about 1 KB gzipped. See section 10 |
| Node engines | >= 18 |
| Module formats | ESM (`vue-star-rate.js`) + UMD (`vue-star-rate.umd.cjs`) + d.ts |
| Accessibility | Keyboard navigation, ARIA group with per-star buttons, `prefers-reduced-motion`. Not audited against WCAG; known gaps are listed in section 11 |
| SSR | safe (all three icon providers render server-side; nothing is loaded asynchronously) |
| Nuxt 3 | compatible — no `<ClientOnly>` wrapper needed |

---

## 2. Installation

```bash
# pnpm (recommended)
pnpm add vue-js-star-rating

# npm
npm install vue-js-star-rating

# yarn
yarn add vue-js-star-rating
```

There are no optional peers: `vue ^3.5.0` is the only peer dependency, and `lucide-vue-next` is not needed. `icon-provider="lucide"` draws Lucide's own star geometry inline as an SVG, so there is nothing to install for it. (Releases 2.0.0 to 3.1.0 are the exception: they import it, so builds fail unless `lucide-vue-next` is installed, see section 10.)

`icon-provider="fontawesome"` renders `<i>` elements with Font Awesome class names, so your app must load Font Awesome's stylesheet itself. Without it the stars are invisible. For example, with `@fortawesome/fontawesome-free` installed in your app:

```bash
pnpm add @fortawesome/fontawesome-free
```

```ts
import '@fortawesome/fontawesome-free/css/all.min.css';
```

---

## 3. Quick start

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { VueStarRate } from 'vue-js-star-rating';
import 'vue-js-star-rating/dist/style.css';

const rating = ref(0);
</script>

<template>
  <VueStarRate v-model="rating" />
</template>
```

### Global plugin registration

```ts
// main.ts
import { createApp } from 'vue';
import App from './App.vue';
import VueStarRatePlugin from 'vue-js-star-rating';
import 'vue-js-star-rating/dist/style.css';

createApp(App).use(VueStarRatePlugin).mount('#app');
```

---

## 4. Props (complete)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` / `modelValue` | `number` | `0` | Current rating value |
| `maxStars` | `number` | `5` | Maximum number of stars |
| `allowHalf` | `boolean` | `false` | Enable 0.5-step ratings |
| `size` | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `'md'` | Size preset (16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 40 px) |
| `iconSize` | `number \| { width: number; height: number }` | auto | Override pixel size |
| `iconProvider` | `'custom' \| 'lucide' \| 'fontawesome'` | `'custom'` | Icon renderer (custom uses the bundled SVG fallback when no slot is provided; fontawesome needs Font Awesome's stylesheet loaded by your app) |
| `colors` | `Partial<StarColors>` | see below | Color configuration |
| `animation` | `Partial<AnimationConfig>` | see below | Animation configuration |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable user interaction (clickable false, focusable true) |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable + grey out the entire component |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a clear button when the rating is above `minRating` (hidden when `readonly` or `disabled`) |
| `allowReset` | `boolean` | `true` | Click the active star again to reset |
| `showCounter` | `boolean` | `false` | Show the rating counter |
| `counterTemplate` | `string` | `'{value} / {max}'` | Counter template; tokens `{value}` and `{max}` are replaced |
| `showTooltip` | `boolean` | `false` | Show `title` tooltips on star hover |
| `tooltipLabels` | `string[]` | — | Custom tooltip text per star (index-based) |
| `minRating` | `number` | `0` | Minimum selectable value |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | Increment step (overridden by `allowHalf`) |
| `rtl` | `boolean` | `false` | Right-to-left layout. Known gap: the half-star fill is still painted on the left side of the star and `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` are not mirrored; pointer clicks on half stars are mirrored |
| `inline` | `boolean` | `false` | Accepted but not implemented (no visual effect) |
| `gap` | `number` | `4` | Gap between stars in pixels |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `'Star rating'` | Accessible group label |
| `className` | `string` | — | Extra CSS class on the root element |
| `faIcons` | `{ empty?: string; filled?: string; half?: string }` | — | FontAwesome class overrides |
| `customIcon` | `CustomIconRenderer` | — | Not implemented: declared in the types, but the component ignores it. Use the `icon` slot instead |

### `StarColors` interface

```ts
interface StarColors {
  empty: string;  // default '#d1d5db'
  filled: string; // default '#fbbf24'
  hover: string;  // default '#f59e0b'
  half?: string;  // default '#fbbf24' (fixed; does not follow a custom filled color)
}
```

### `AnimationConfig` interface

```ts
interface AnimationConfig {
  enabled: boolean;                                 // default true
  duration: number;                                 // default 200 ms
  type: 'scale' | 'bounce' | 'pulse' | 'none';      // default 'scale'
}
```

The hover animations are switched off when the user has `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` set at the OS level.

`enabled: false` and `type: 'none'` are not a full off-switch: on interactive stars the base hover transition and `scale(1.1)` remain unless the user prefers reduced motion. Because of that base scale, `type: 'scale'` (1.2) only differs from `'none'` on read-only and disabled stars, which have no base hover scale and so do stop animating with `enabled: false`; `'bounce'` and `'pulse'` play on hover for every star.

---

## 5. Events

| Event | Payload | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `number` | Emitted whenever the committed rating changes through the component (click, keyboard, `setRating()`, `reset()`); not emitted when the parent itself changes `v-model` |
| `change` | `(value: number, oldValue: number)` | Emitted right after `update:modelValue`, on the same occasions (click, keyboard, `setRating()`, `reset()`); external `v-model` writes do not re-emit |
| `hover` | `number \| null` | Previewed value while the pointer is over the stars; `null` when it leaves them |
| `focus` | `()` | Root element received focus (not emitted when focus lands directly on a star button) |
| `blur` | `()` | Root element lost focus (also emitted when focus moves onto a star button inside it) |

---

## 6. Slots

| Slot | Scoped props | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `{ filled, half, size, color, index }` | Custom icon per star (used when `iconProvider="custom"`) |
| `counter` | `{ value, max }` | Custom counter content |
| `clear` | — | Custom clear button content |

---

## 7. Keyboard navigation

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `→`, `↑` | Increase rating by step |
| `←`, `↓` | Decrease rating by step |
| `Home` | Set to `minRating` |
| `End` | Set to `maxStars` |
| `1`–`9` | Jump to numeric value (ignored when greater than `maxStars`) |
| `0` | Reset to `minRating` |

---

## 8. Exposed methods

```ts
const star = ref<InstanceType<typeof VueStarRate>>();

star.value?.reset();          // back to initial value
star.value?.setRating(3.5);   // set programmatically (with the default step and no allowHalf, 3.5 snaps to 4)
star.value?.getRating();      // current value
star.value?.focus();          // focus the root element
star.value?.blur();           // remove focus
```

---

## 9. Composable — `useStarRating`

Headless API exported alongside the component:

```ts
import { useStarRating } from 'vue-js-star-rating';

const {
  stars,         // computed StarItem[]
  displayRating, // computed number (hover-aware)
  isHovering,
  isFocused,
  handleClick,
  handleMouseEnter,
  handleMouseLeave,
  handleKeyDown,
  reset,
  setRating,
  getRating,
  setFocused,
} = useStarRating(options, emit);
```

Options accept `MaybeRefOrGetter<T>` for full reactivity.

---

## 10. Bundle composition

Both entry files (ESM and UMD) import only `vue` and contain all three icon providers: the built-in SVG star, Lucide's star (drawn inline) and the Font Awesome `<i>` renderer. Nothing is lazy-loaded: there is no dynamic `import()`, no async chunk and no per-provider code splitting. Measured with Vite 6 and esbuild minification, `vue` external, gzip -9:

| Import | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| `import { VueStarRate } from 'vue-js-star-rating'` | about 12.4 KB raw / 4.6 KB gzipped JavaScript, plus 2.9 KB raw / 0.75 KB gzipped CSS (`vue-js-star-rating/dist/style.css`) |
| `import { useStarRating } from 'vue-js-star-rating'` | about 1 KB gzipped JavaScript |

Export-level tree-shaking works, which is why `useStarRating` alone is small. There is no component-level code splitting: importing `VueStarRate` includes all three icon providers, whichever `iconProvider` you use.

History: version 3.1.0 claimed lazy-loaded icon chunks and documented `lucide-vue-next` as an optional peer. That was wrong. Its entry file contained `import("lucide-vue-next")`, which bundlers resolve at build time, so Vite, webpack, esbuild, Nuxt and Storybook builds fail unless `lucide-vue-next` is installed (GitHub issue #13; issue #7 had been closed earlier with the same wrong claim). This is fixed in 3.1.1; see CHANGELOG.md.

---

## 11. Accessibility notes

- Container: `role="group"` + `aria-label` (configurable via `ariaLabel`); `aria-disabled` reflects the `disabled` prop; `tabindex="0"` for keyboard focus (`-1` when disabled).
- Stars: each is a `<button type="button">` with `aria-pressed` reflecting state and an `aria-label` describing the star value (for example "3 stars"). The buttons are `disabled` when the component is `readonly` or `disabled`; read-only is conveyed this way because `aria-readonly` is not valid on `role="group"` and is not used.
- Counter: `aria-live="polite"` for live announcements (rendered only when `showCounter` is on).
- Keyboard: arrow keys (by `step`, or 0.5 with `allowHalf`), `Home`, `End` and the digits `0`–`9` set the rating. Ctrl, Alt and Meta key combinations are left to the browser; `Tab` and any other non-rating key never change the value.
- Focus indicator: the container shows `outline: 2px solid var(--star-color-filled)` on `:focus-visible`; the star buttons show the browser's default focus ring on keyboard focus.
- Motion: hover scale / bounce / pulse animations are wrapped in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`.

The package has not been audited against WCAG, so it makes no conformance claim. Known gaps:

- The default star colors have low contrast on white: the empty color `#d1d5db` is 1.47:1 and the filled color `#fbbf24` is 1.67:1. Pass your own `colors`.
- `size="xs"` targets are 16 px, below the 24 px target-size minimum of WCAG 2.2.
- A half value such as 2.5 is announced to a screen reader like the next whole number, because the half star is `aria-pressed` like a full one.
- The numeric value is only available as text when `showCounter` is on.

---

## 12. Frequently asked questions

**Do I need `lucide-vue-next` if I use FontAwesome or a custom icon?**
No. `vue-js-star-rating` has no runtime dependencies and its only peer dependency is `vue` (`^3.5.0`); there are no optional peers. `iconProvider="lucide"` draws Lucide's own star geometry inline as an SVG, so there is nothing to install for it. `iconProvider="fontawesome"` renders `<i>` elements with Font Awesome class names, so your app must load Font Awesome's stylesheet itself, for example `import '@fortawesome/fontawesome-free/css/all.min.css'`; without it the stars are invisible. The exception is releases 2.0.0 to 3.1.0, which imported `lucide-vue-next` at build time (3.1.0 also wrongly documented it as an optional peer), so Vite, webpack, esbuild, Nuxt and Storybook builds fail unless it is installed (GitHub issue #13). This is fixed in 3.1.1; see CHANGELOG.md.

**Is it SSR-safe?**
Yes. The component renders deterministically on the server, and the markup of all three icon providers (default SVG, Lucide, Font Awesome) is part of the server-rendered HTML. Nothing is loaded asynchronously, so no `<ClientOnly>` or `<Suspense>` wrapper is needed.

**Does it work with Nuxt 3?**
Yes. No `<ClientOnly>` or `<Suspense>` wrapper is needed: nothing is loaded asynchronously and every icon provider renders on the server.

**What is the bundle size?**
Measured with Vite 6 and esbuild minification, `vue` external, gzip -9: `import { VueStarRate }` costs about 12.4 KB raw / 4.6 KB gzipped of JavaScript plus 2.9 KB raw / 0.75 KB gzipped of CSS (`vue-js-star-rating/dist/style.css`). All three icon providers are inside that one entry file; nothing is lazy-loaded or split into chunks. `useStarRating` alone costs about 1 KB gzipped because export-level tree-shaking works; there is no component-level code splitting.

**Can I use it without `v-model`?**
Yes. Pass `:model-value` and listen to `@update:modelValue` (or `@change`). The `useStarRating` composable is exported for headless usage.

**Is it tree-shakeable?**
Yes, at export level. `sideEffects` is set to `**/*.css` only, so unused named exports are eliminated: importing only `useStarRating` costs about 1 KB gzipped (measured with Vite 6 and esbuild minification). There is no component-level code splitting: importing `VueStarRate` always brings all three icon providers, whichever `iconProvider` you use.

**Which Vue versions are supported?**
Vue 3.5+. The component uses `defineModel`, `useTemplateRef`, and `MaybeRefOrGetter`. Vue 2 is not supported.

---

## 13. Migration

### v3.0 → v3.1

- 3.1.0 documented lazy-loaded icon providers and `lucide-vue-next` as an optional peer. That was wrong: no separate icon chunks were emitted, and the 3.1.0 entry file contains `import("lucide-vue-next")`, so Vite, webpack, esbuild, Nuxt and Storybook builds fail unless it is installed (GitHub issue #13). This is fixed in 3.1.1; see section 10 and CHANGELOG.md.

### v2 → v3

- `lucideIcons` prop → `iconProvider="lucide"`
- `role="slider"` → `role="group"`
- `animation.scale: 1.15` → `animation.type: 'scale'`
- Vue peer raised from `^3.3.0` → `^3.5.0`
